sentences.text:
!For Petitioner : Mr.B.Saravanan  ^For Respondents : Mr.K.Chellapandian,
 Additional Advocate General  Assist.by Mr.Aayiram K.Selvakumar :ORDER

The petitioner was working as a Sanitary Inspector in Thirukalukundram Town Panchayat,
Kanchipuram District in the year 2009.
Then, he was appointed as a Food Inspector in the year 2011 as he completed Food Inspector training in the year 2010.
In the meanwhile, the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 came into force.
The petitioner was appointed as a Food Safety Officer by the Commissioner of Food Safety vide notification dated 01.12.2011.
The said notification was also duly published in the Gazette.
The petitioner has been working as a Food Safety Officer ever since.
By order dated 15.02.2018, he has been relieved to his parent department with effect from 20.02.2018.
Relieving order was also issued on 19.02.2018.
The said orders are under challenge on a host of legal grounds.

The petitioner herein also questions the jurisdiction of the Commissioner of Food Safety,
Chennai to issue the impugned orders.

2.Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Additional Advocate General assisted by the learned Additional Government Pleader for the respondents.
3.This Court is of the view that the issue on hand can be resolved by holding that the order in question is bad for non compliance with the principles of natural justice.
The other issues can very well be left open.
Admittedly, the pay drawn by the Food Safety Officer is higher than the pay drawn by the Food Inspector or Sanitary Inspector.
On account of the impugned order, the petitioner would certainly suffer pay reduction.
Thus, there is a civil consequence involved.
4.It is also seen that the impugned orders have been passed as a punitive measure.
It appears that the authorities are not happy with the performance of the petitioner and it necessitated the passing of the impugned orders.

This Court has consistently held that when an administrative order casts some stigma or shadow on the employee concerned, the authority concerned will have to proceed by issuing a notice the concerned employee.
5.In this case, the principles of natural justice will have to be followed at least to a summary extent.
In other words, notice will have to be given and the explanation of the petitioner obtained.
Since this basic requirement has not been complied with, this Court has to quash the impugned orders on this ground.
Accordingly, the orders impugned in this writ petition stand quashed.
It is made clear that this Court has not gone into any other aspect of the matter.
All the issues are left open.
6.This Writ Petition is allowed to the extent as indicated above.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
